facebook.content_angle: Stroke rate vs stroke length — the speed equation most club swimmers get backwards, and how finding your personal optimal balance unlocks faster splits without more effort
facebook.post_text:
Stroke faster and you'll swim faster. Right? ⚡

Wrong. Most club swimmers crank up their stroke rate when they want to go harder — and bleed speed doing it.

Here's what's actually happening:

👉 Higher stroke rate without matching distance-per-stroke means shorter, weaker pulls and more energy burned per metre
👉 Elite 100m freestyle swimmers average 85–95cm of distance per stroke — most club swimmers sit 15–20cm below that
👉 The fastest split isn't found by churning harder — it's found by holding length under fatigue

That 15–20cm gap? Over 100m it costs you 10–14 additional strokes. That's energy you didn't have to spend. 💥

This is the stroke equation worth obsessing over:

✔️ Drill for length first — use a tempo trainer set slow and hold your distance per stroke
✔️ Then gradually increase rate while protecting that length
✔️ Find the crossover point where both are high — that's your personal speed ceiling

Are you training stroke rate, stroke length — or have you found your balance?
